text: In an AlphaFold2 prediction, two well-folded domains connected by a flexible linker would typically show which combination of confidence metrics?
choices: High pLDDT within each domain, but high PAE (predicted aligned error) between the domains
Low pLDDT throughout both domains and low PAE between them
High pLDDT throughout and low PAE between domains, indicating a fixed relative orientation
Low pLDDT within domains but high inter-domain PAE
explanation: Each domain folds confidently and independently, so per-residue pLDDT is high within each domain, while the flexible linker means AlphaFold2 cannot confidently place one domain relative to the other, producing high inter-domain PAE. Low pLDDT throughout would instead suggest both domains themselves are poorly modeled or disordered, and low inter-domain PAE (option C) is what you would see for a rigid, confidently-oriented multi-domain protein, not a flexible one.
